key_insight: Although this paper is about a disordered double perovskite rather than a solar cell, its central finding is that B-site antisite disorder in Sr2FeRuO6 stabilizes Griffiths-like magnetic clusters and strongly localized charge transport.
engineering_relevance: The results highlight how structural disorder and cation mixing can profoundly alter magnetic and transport behavior in oxide materials, informing defect-aware design of functional perovskites for spintronic and electronic applications.
method: Monoclinic structure analysis of Sr2FeRuO6 with significant B-site antisite disorder
Magnetic measurements to identify a Griffiths phase and short-range ferromagnetic clusters
Electrical transport analysis comparing small-polaron hopping and variable-range hopping regimes
evidence_signal: The abstract reports robust Griffiths-phase behavior above the magnetic ordering temperature and a clear temperature-dependent transport crossover from small-polaron hopping to variable-range hopping.
watch_item: Because the conclusions rely on disordered bulk oxide behavior, performance and reproducibility may be highly sensitive to sample stoichiometry, antisite disorder level, and synthesis conditions.
paper_title: Disorder-Induced Griffiths like Phase and Charge Localization in Sr2FeRuO6
